meta.titre: Sedimentary Rock Types and Textures: classifying clastic rocks and reading grain properties

sections.contenu_markdown: A builder in Douala or Yaounde who buys sand and gravel for concrete is handling the raw material of sedimentary rocks. Sand, pebbles and mud collect in rivers, lakes and the sea, and when they are buried they harden into sandstone, conglomerate and shale. A geologist reads the size, shape and sorting of the grains as a record of how far and how violently they travelled. Examiners ask for the characteristics of the main rock groups and for exact definitions of terms such as sorting, roundness and maturity. This course gives you the classification and the vocabulary to answer both.

items: Sediments are made by weathering and erosion and are moved by water, wind and ice.
Lithification turns loose sediment into rock by compaction and cementation.
Quartz is hard and chemically resistant, while feldspar and clay minerals weather more easily.
Grain size is measured in millimetres, and one millimetre is one thousandth of a metre.

sections.titre: Clastic sedimentary rocks: grain size, rock groups and texture
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Classification by grain size (Wentworth scale)
| Grain class | Diameter | Rock group | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clay | below 0.004 mm | Argillaceous | claystone, shale |
| Silt | 0.004 to 0.0625 mm | Argillaceous | siltstone, mudstone |
| Sand | 0.0625 to 2 mm | Arenaceous | sandstone |
| Granule to boulder | above 2 mm | Rudaceous | conglomerate, breccia |

Sand is subdivided into very fine (0.0625 to 0.125 mm), fine (0.125 to 0.25 mm), medium (0.25 to 0.5 mm), coarse (0.5 to 1 mm) and very coarse (1 to 2 mm).

### Main clastic rocks
- **Conglomerate** has rounded clasts in a finer matrix, so the clasts travelled far. **Breccia** has angular clasts, so they travelled only a short way from the source.
- **Quartz arenite** is almost pure quartz sand, well sorted and rounded, often cemented by silica. **Arkose** is quartz with a large proportion of feldspar, usually from granite eroded and buried quickly. **Greywacke** is a dark, poorly sorted sandstone with angular grains and rock fragments in a clay-rich matrix, often laid down by turbidity currents.
- **Shale** splits into thin sheets (it is fissile); **mudstone** breaks into blocks. Both are fine grained, usually laminated, and have very low permeability because flat clay particles pack tightly.

### Texture terms
- **Sorting** is the spread of grain sizes. Grains of similar size are well sorted (typical of wind and beach sand); a wide range of sizes is poorly sorted (typical of rapid deposition, as in debris flows or glacial deposits).
- **Roundness** is the sharpness of the corners and edges of a grain. It increases with the distance and time of transport.
- **Sphericity** is how closely the overall shape of a grain approaches a sphere. A grain can be well rounded but elongate, so it has low sphericity.
- **Maturity** is how far a sediment has been worked toward a stable end product. Textural maturity increases as clay matrix is lost, sorting improves and grains round. Mineralogical maturity increases as unstable minerals (feldspar, mica, rock fragments) are destroyed, leaving quartz.
- **Matrix** is fine sediment deposited with the grains; **cement** is a mineral (silica, calcite or iron oxide) precipitated later in the pore spaces.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to give an account of the characteristics of arenaceous, rudaceous or argillaceous rocks.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use a fixed plan: grain size and composition; texture (sorting, roundness, matrix or cement); structures (bedding, cross-bedding, lamination, fissility, fossils); the usual environment of deposition; named examples and one use. A list of rock names alone earns few marks, so every heading needs a statement about that rock group.

variantes.nom: Reading texture from a description or thin section
variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question describes grains or shows a thin section with a scale bar.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Compare the largest and smallest grains with the scale to give the size range. Say whether most grains fall in one size class (well sorted) or in several (poorly sorted). Note the amount of clay matrix and the sharpness of the corners. Then link to history: well sorted, rounded, matrix-free grains suggest long transport and reworking; poorly sorted, angular grains with much matrix suggest short transport and rapid burial.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When several terms are to be discussed for a few marks each.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give a one-line definition, then a contrast or example: sphericity describes overall shape, whereas roundness describes the sharpness of corners, so a flat pebble can be well rounded yet of low sphericity. Three terms for six marks means about two marks each: one for the definition and one for the explanation or example.

sections.enonce_markdown: Give an account of the characteristics of argillaceous rocks. (8 marks)

etapes.justification: Give an account means describe the features in an organised way and not merely name the rocks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan: (1) grain size and composition, (2) texture and structures, (3) physical properties, (4) environment of deposition, (5) examples.

etapes.justification: Argillaceous is defined by the finest grain sizes, so this is the first mark.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Grains are silt and clay (below 0.0625 mm), made mainly of clay minerals with some fine quartz. Individual grains cannot be seen with the naked eye.

etapes.justification: Fine grains settle slowly from suspension and give distinctive structures.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Thin laminations; shale is fissile and splits into sheets, while mudstone breaks into blocks. Colour varies: grey or black with organic matter, red or brown with iron oxide.

etapes.justification: Properties follow from the flat, tightly packed clay particles.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Soft and easily scratched; low permeability, so the rock acts as a seal or aquiclude for water and oil.

etapes.justification: Linking rock to setting shows interpretation, which earns the final marks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Deposited from suspension in low-energy settings such as lagoons, lakes, floodplains and deep water; may contain fossils. Examples: shale, mudstone, siltstone, claystone.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Model answer.** Argillaceous rocks are the finest-grained clastic rocks, made of silt and clay particles smaller than 0.0625 mm, mainly clay minerals with some fine quartz. They are laminated, and shale splits easily into thin sheets (fissile) whereas mudstone breaks into blocks. They are soft and have very low permeability because the flat particles are packed tightly, so they form seals. Colour depends on composition: dark rocks contain organic matter and red or brown rocks contain iron oxide. They are deposited from suspension in quiet, low-energy water such as lagoons, lakes, floodplains and deep seas, and they may contain fossils. Examples are shale, mudstone, siltstone and claystone.

items.erreur_markdown: Roundness and sphericity mean the same thing.
items.pourquoi_faux: Roundness describes the sharpness of the corners and edges. Sphericity describes how close the whole grain is to a sphere. A long, smooth pebble is well rounded but has low sphericity.
items.correction_markdown: Define each term separately and give one contrast, such as a smooth but elongate pebble.

items.erreur_markdown: Breccia is made of rounded pebbles.
items.pourquoi_faux: Breccia has angular clasts, which shows short transport. Rounded clasts make a conglomerate.
items.correction_markdown: Write that breccia has angular clasts and conglomerate has rounded clasts.

items.erreur_markdown: A well sorted sediment contains grains of many different sizes.
items.pourquoi_faux: This is the meaning of poorly sorted. Well sorted means that most grains are close to one size.
items.correction_markdown: Write that well sorted means a narrow range of grain sizes.

items.pourquoi_faux: Arkose is rich in feldspar, an unstable mineral that is destroyed by long weathering and transport, so it is mineralogically immature. A mature sandstone is a quartz arenite.
items.correction_markdown: Write that arkose is immature and that quartz arenite is the most mature sandstone.

items.erreur_markdown: Cement and matrix are the same thing.
items.pourquoi_faux: Matrix is fine sediment deposited with the grains. Cement is a mineral precipitated later from groundwater in the pores.
items.correction_markdown: Say that matrix is deposited at the same time as the grains and cement is added after burial.

items.enonce_markdown: Classify each grain by size class and rock group (rudaceous, arenaceous or argillaceous): (a) 0.3 mm; (b) 0.01 mm; (c) 12 mm; (d) 0.002 mm.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Medium sand, arenaceous** (0.25 to 0.5 mm). (b) **Silt, argillaceous** (0.004 to 0.0625 mm). (c) **Pebble, rudaceous** (above 2 mm). (d) **Clay, argillaceous** (below 0.004 mm). Award a mark for each correct pair.

items.enonce_markdown: A rock contains sharp-cornered clasts between 3 mm and 40 mm across, set in a matrix of sand. (a) Name the rock and its group. (b) Describe the sorting. (c) What does the shape of the clasts suggest about transport and deposition?
items.solution_markdown: (a) Clasts above 2 mm make it **rudaceous**; with angular clasts it is a **breccia**. (b) The largest clasts are about 13 times the size of the smallest (40 / 3), a very wide range, plus a sand matrix, so the rock is **poorly sorted**. (c) Sharp corners show **short transport** from a nearby source, and the poor sorting and matrix show **rapid deposition** with little reworking.

items.enonce_markdown: Three sandstones are described. X: 97% quartz, rounded grains, well sorted, no clay matrix. Y: 60% quartz and 30% feldspar, angular grains, moderately sorted. Z: 50% quartz and 15% rock fragments, angular grains, poorly sorted, with a dark clay-rich matrix. (a) Name each rock. (b) Rank them from most to least mature. (c) Explain what the differences suggest about transport and source.
items.solution_markdown: (a) X is a **quartz arenite**, Y is an **arkose**, Z is a **greywacke**. (b) Most mature **X**, then **Y**, least mature **Z**: X has lost its matrix and unstable minerals, Y still contains much feldspar, and Z is poorly sorted, rich in matrix and rich in rock fragments. (c) X was transported far or reworked repeatedly, for example on a beach or in a desert, which rounded and sorted the grains and removed feldspar and clay. Y came from a granite source and was eroded and buried quickly before the feldspar could weather. Z was deposited rapidly, close to its source, with fine and coarse material together, for example from a turbidity current. Award a mark for each correct name, for the ranking and for a reasoned point on each rock.

items_markdown: Clastic rocks are classified by grain size: rudaceous above 2 mm, arenaceous 0.0625 to 2 mm, argillaceous below 0.0625 mm.
Conglomerate has rounded clasts and breccia has angular clasts; quartz arenite, arkose and greywacke are the main sandstones.
Sorting is the spread of grain sizes; roundness is the sharpness of corners; sphericity is overall shape.
Maturity increases with loss of clay matrix, better sorting and rounding, and the destruction of unstable minerals.
Matrix is deposited with the grains, cement is precipitated afterwards.
An account question needs grain size, composition, texture, structures, environment and examples.
